About the Team
 
The security team at Meesho is like the Avengers to Meesho's S.H.I.E.L.D. After all, when 5% of Indian households shop with us, it’s important to build resilient systems to manage millions of orders every day. We’ve done this – with zero downtime! 😎 Sounds impossible? Well, that’s the kind of Engineering muscle that has helped Meesho become the e-commerce giant it is today. We value speed over perfection, and see failures as opportunities to become better. We’ve taken steps to inculcate a strong ‘Founder’s Mindset’ across our engineering teams, making us grow and move fast. We place special emphasis on the continuous growth of each team member - and we do this with regular 1-1s and open communication. As a Security Engineer, you will be part of self-starters who thrive on teamwork and constructive feedback. We know how to party as hard as we work! If we aren’t building unparalleled tech solutions, you can find us debating the plot points of our favorite books and games – or even gossiping over chai. So, if a day filled with building impactful solutions with a fun team sounds appealing to you, join us.
 
About the Role
 
As a Security Engineer 3 in Infrastructure Security, you are a senior individual contributor who owns Meesho's infrastructure security and security operations (SOC) end to end. You will be one of the engineers securing everything from GCP organisation policy and IAM down to Kubernetes workloads and CI/CD infrastructure, so you will set the technical direction for infrastructure security, not just execute it. You operate with limited supervision, act as the trusted security voice in infrastructure and platform architecture discussions, and partner closely with other engineers whom you will mentor and uplevel. 
The role rewards breadth with depth: you should be comfortable moving between cloud architecture reviews, hands-on hardening, detection engineering, and incident response in the same week, and you will have unusual freedom to automate, consolidate, and build the guardrails that let a lean team secure a platform operating at Meesho's scale.




What you will do
Cloud Security Architecture & Design Review: Own secure design for Meesho's GCP estate, including organisation policies, project structure, IAM and service-account hygiene, VPC design, VPC Service Controls, workload identity, and encryption/key management (Cloud KMS). Lead threat modeling and security reviews for new infrastructure and platform services, and drive the resulting requirements into production with platform engineering.

Kubernetes & Container Security: Harden GKE clusters and containerised workloads end to end: cluster configuration, RBAC, network policies, admission control and policy-as-code, workload identity, image provenance and registry controls, and runtime posture. Define the secure-by-default patterns that platform and product teams build on.

Identity & Zero Trust: Drive Meesho's zero-trust roadmap for infrastructure: least-privilege IAM at scale, elimination of long-lived credentials and static keys, just-in-time and break-glass access patterns, secrets management, and strong isolation between production and non-production environments.

Posture Management & Hardening: Own cloud security posture management using GCP-native tooling (Security Command Center) and complementary controls. Continuously find, prioritise, and burn down misconfigurations and attack paths across the estate, and convert recurring findings into preventive guardrails rather than tickets.

Infrastructure as Code & Pipeline Security: Embed security into how infrastructure ships: IaC scanning and policy enforcement (Terraform), CI/CD pipeline hardening, artifact and dependency integrity, and software supply-chain controls for infrastructure components.

SOC & Detection and Response (End-to-End Ownership): Own Meesho's SOC and detection & response function: run the SIEM and the managed detection (MxDR) partner relationship, own alert triage quality, escalation paths, and on-call, and ensure infrastructure telemetry (cloud audit logs, Kubernetes audit, network and identity signals) is onboarded and high-signal. Build and tune detections for cloud-native attack techniques, lead incident response as the senior technical responder, and drive post-incident fixes to architectural closure.

Security Automation: Design and build automation that multiplies a lean team: auto-remediation for common misconfigurations, access-review tooling, inventory and attack-surface mapping, and self-service security workflows for engineering teams.

Vulnerability & Patch Management: Own the vulnerability lifecycle for infrastructure: OS and image patching posture, container base-image management, exposure tracking, and remediation SLAs, with metrics that drive engineering prioritisation.

AI Infrastructure Security: Contribute to securing the infrastructure behind Meesho's AI workloads, including the AI gateway plane, model-access controls, and isolation and egress controls for agents and AI services running in production.

Mentorship & Security Partnership: Mentor the SE2 on the team, review their work, and raise the team's technical bar. Act as the infrastructure security subject-matter expert for platform, SRE, and DevOps teams, influencing decisions without direct authority.

Compliance Enablement: Translate control requirements from frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, the DPDP Act, and CERT-In directions (logging, retention, incident reporting) into pragmatic technical controls, and provide evidence from systems you own.

What you will need
Experience: 5-7 years of hands-on experience in infrastructure, cloud, or platform security, with a demonstrated track record of owning security outcomes end to end in a production cloud environment.

Education: A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field is preferred.

Core Technical Depth:

• 

Strong hands-on cloud security experience, ideally on GCP (IAM, organisation policy, VPC and VPC Service Controls, Cloud KMS, Security Command Center, audit logging); deep AWS or Azure experience with willingness to go deep on GCP also works.

• 

Deep, practical Kubernetes security expertise (ideally GKE): RBAC, network policies, admission control, workload identity, image and registry security, and runtime threat detection.

• 

Proven ability to lead threat modeling for complex distributed infrastructure and translate findings into controls that ship.

• 

Hands-on experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform) and with embedding security scanning and policy enforcement into CI/CD.

• 

Strong scripting or programming ability (Python or Go preferred) and a bias toward building automation over running manual reviews.

• 

Hands-on experience running detection and response: operating a SIEM (ideally with a managed SOC/MxDR partner), knowing what telemetry matters, writing high-signal detections, and leading infrastructure security incidents to closure.

• 

Solid grounding in Linux, networking, and identity fundamentals (OAuth/OIDC, SAML, service identity).

General Skills & Acumen:

• 

Sound judgment on risk prioritisation at scale: knowing which of a thousand findings actually matter and why.

• 

Comfort operating in a lean team: self-directed, pragmatic about scope, and able to drive initiatives to closure across platform, SRE, and DevOps teams without direct authority.

• 

Excellent communication skills, able to explain infrastructure risk to both engineers and leadership.

• 

Ability and willingness to mentor an earlier-career security engineer.

Bonus Points

• 

Relevant certifications such as CKS (Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist), Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer, OSCP, or GCPN.

• 

Experience with zero-trust architecture rollouts or large-scale IAM remediation programmes.

•

e736c2fa0492a640.description: **The short version** MnemioAI gives every employee an AI agent that works in the apps they already use and learns how they work. Your job is to make those agents genuinely useful inside real businesses: sit with a team, find the work that costs them the most, and replace it with agents that are accurate enough to trust. You'll be half engineer, half business analyst. The engineering gets the agent working. The business sense decides which work is worth automating first. **The bar: better than AI, using AI** Give a capable model a task with no context and you get a plausible, average answer. Give the same model the right data, the business's rules, examples of good and bad output, tools that check its work, and someone who knows where it tends to fail, and the result is a different class of work. That difference is the job. We judge the work on one question: is what the agent produces with your setup clearly better than what the customer would get by asking the model directly? Better means more accurate, closer to how this particular business works, and finished enough that a person approves it instead of redoing it. In practice, that means being comfortable with the unglamorous parts: reading the data before writing a prompt, building evaluations, testing the edge cases, and saying "the model can't do this reliably yet" when that's true. **What you'll do** Map how work actually happens in a customer's finance, operations or sales team, including the steps nobody wrote down. Rank processes by hours lost, errors and money at risk, against the effort to automate them. Start with the ones that pay back in days. Build the automations on MnemioAI: connect tools through APIs and MCP, write the agent's instructions and skills, add approval steps so people stay in control, and handle the messy cases. Measure the outcome (hours saved, errors caught, cash recovered) and report it in language a business owner understands. Bring patterns back to the product team, so the fifth customer gets in a day what the first one took a week to get. **What a good week looks like** On Monday you sit with a finance manager who spends nine hours a week matching supplier invoices to purchase orders and delivery notes. By Thursday an agent does the matching overnight and flags the six that don't line up, with the reason for each. She clears them in twenty minutes. On Friday you write down what you learned, so the next customer with the same problem is live in a day. **Problems you'll work on** Matching invoices against purchase orders and delivery logs, then preparing bills in QuickBooks, Xero or Tally for approval Reconciling marketplace payouts against orders, fees and refunds, and drafting claims for money owed Turning CRM, ad-platform and finance data into a weekly management report, with the commentary drafted Chasing overdue invoices in each client's channel and tone, and knowing when to hand over to a person Answering employees' questions from the company's own documents and Slack history, with sources What we're looking for 2–5 years building software, automation or data workflows in Python or TypeScript, with real APIs, webhooks and messy data Hands-on work with large language models: prompting, tool use or agents, evaluation, and a clear sense of where they fail Evidence that you get better results from AI than the default: a project, a before-and-after, an evaluation set, anything you can show us Business sense: you can sit with a finance or operations lead, understand the process quickly and tell which problem to solve first A bias for return on effort: a two-day automation that saves ten hours a week beats a three-month project that might Clear writing and speaking in English, and patience explaining technical trade-offs to non-technical people **Nice to have** Building MCP servers or integrations for business software **You'll probably enjoy this if** You've always been more interested in why a process is broken than in which tool fixes it You check a model's output before you trust it, and enjoy working out why it was wrong You like seeing real people use your work in the same week you built it Apply here directly: https://mnemioai.com/careers/ai-automation-engineer
